title: Boss: secure mail for a team
summary: Audit key sizes, wrap keys with RSA, encrypt one message to many recipients, and sign sealed letters so forgeries never decrypt.

steps.title: The brief
body: Your team needs encrypted mail between colleagues. Build it in four pieces, each tested on its own: a key-size audit for the config, RSA key wrapping for legacy recipients, one message encrypted for several recipients at once, and signed, sealed letters where a forgery is rejected *before* anything is decrypted.
Keys and signatures are random, so the tests check behaviour (round trips, rejections, lengths), never values.

steps.title: Audit the key config
prompt: Read lines like `RSA 2048` from standard input until the end, and print one verdict per line using the policy from lesson 5:
```text
RSA 2048: 112 bits, legacy
EC 256: 128 bits, good
RSA 1024: 80 bits, weak

Rules: `AES` is its key size; `RSA` uses the thresholds 15360/7680/3072/2048/1024 for 256/192/128/112/80 bits (else 0); `EC` is `min(bits / 2, 256)`. Verdict: under 112 `weak`, under 128 `legacy`, otherwise `good`. An unknown algorithm prints `<line>: unknown algorithm`. Skip blank lines.
steps.starter: // Read lines with Console.ReadLine() until null.
hints: Check RSA thresholds from the largest down.

steps.title: RSA key wrapping
prompt: Some recipients only have RSA keys. Write:
- `byte[] WrapKey(RSA recipient, byte[] aesKey)`: throw `ArgumentException` unless the key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes; otherwise OAEP-SHA256 encrypt it.
- `byte[] UnwrapKey(RSA recipient, byte[] wrapped)`: OAEP-SHA256 decrypt; throw `ArgumentException` if the result is not 16, 24 or 32 bytes.
A wrong private key must fail with a `CryptographicException` (let RSA throw it).
solution: bool ValidKeySize(int n) => n is 16 or 24 or 32;
if (!ValidKeySize(aesKey.Length)) throw new ArgumentException("An AES key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes.");
if (!ValidKeySize(key.Length)) throw new ArgumentException("The unwrapped value is not an AES key.");
template: {{CODE}}
using var dojoBob = System.Security.Cryptography.RSA.Create(2048);
using var dojoEve = System.Security.Cryptography.RSA.Create(2048);
var dojoKey = System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32);
var dojoWrapped = WrapKey(dojoBob, dojoKey);
Dojo.Eq("a wrapped key is 256 bytes", 256, dojoWrapped.Length);
Dojo.Eq("unwrapping gives the key back", dojoKey, UnwrapKey(dojoBob, dojoWrapped));
Dojo.Eq("a 16-byte key works too", 16, UnwrapKey(dojoBob, WrapKey(dojoBob, new byte[16])).Length);
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a 20-byte key is refused", () => WrapKey(dojoBob, new byte[20]));
Dojo.Throws<System.Security.Cryptography.CryptographicException>("the wrong private key fails", () => UnwrapKey(dojoEve, dojoWrapped));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a wrapped non-key is refused", () => UnwrapKey(dojoBob, dojoBob.Encrypt(new byte[5], System.Security.Cryptography.RSAEncryptionPadding.OaepSHA256)));
hints: `n is 16 or 24 or 32` checks the size in one expression.
Do the size check before encrypting, and again after decrypting.

steps.title: One message, many recipients
prompt: Encrypt a message **once** and let several people open it, the way PGP and JWE do:
`(byte[] Body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> Keys) SealForMany(byte[] message, Dictionary<string, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey> recipients)`
- one random 32-byte content key; `Body = [nonce 12][tag 16][ciphertext]` with AES-GCM;

- for **each** recipient, wrap the content key with ephemeral ECDH: `[eph public key 91][nonce 12][tag 16][wrapped key 32]` (151 bytes), AES key = HKDF-SHA256 of the shared secret, 32 bytes, info = UTF-8 `"dojo-mail-wrap:" + name` (so a wrap cannot be moved to another name).

`byte[]? OpenAs(string name, ECDiffieHellman me, byte[] body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys)`: return `null` if `name` has no entry or any decryption fails (catch `CryptographicException`); otherwise the message.
starter: (byte[] Body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> Keys) SealForMany(byte[] message, Dictionary<string, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey> recipients)
byte[]? OpenAs(string name, ECDiffieHellman me, byte[] body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys)
solution: (byte[] Ciphertext, byte[] Nonce, byte[] Tag) GcmSeal(byte[] key, byte[] plain)
byte[] GcmOpen(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] tag, byte[] cipher)
(byte[] Body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> Keys) SealForMany(byte[] message, Dictionary<string, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey> recipients)
byte[] wrapKey = HKDF.DeriveKey(HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, eph.DeriveRawSecretAgreement(publicKey), 32, null, WrapLabel(name));
byte[]? OpenAs(string name, ECDiffieHellman me, byte[] body, Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys)
if (!keys.TryGetValue(name, out var entry) || entry.Length != 151 || body.Length < 28) return null;
byte[] contentKey = GcmOpen(wrapKey, entry[91..103], entry[103..119], entry[119..]);
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoCurve = System.Security.Cryptography.ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256;
using var dojoAda = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoBen = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoCy = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoEve = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
var dojoMsg = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("Offsite moved to Thursday.");
var dojoTo = new Dictionary<string, System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey> { ["ada"] = dojoAda.PublicKey, ["ben"] = dojoBen.PublicKey, ["cy"] = dojoCy.PublicKey };
var (dojoBody, dojoKeys) = SealForMany(dojoMsg, dojoTo);
Dojo.Eq("the body is 28 bytes plus the message", 28 + dojoMsg.Length, dojoBody.Length);
Dojo.Eq("one wrapped key per recipient", 3, dojoKeys.Count);
Dojo.Check("each wrapped key is 151 bytes", dojoKeys.Values.All(k => k.Length == 151), "a wrapped key has the wrong size");
Dojo.Eq("ada opens it", dojoMsg, OpenAs("ada", dojoAda, dojoBody, dojoKeys));
Dojo.Eq("ben opens it", dojoMsg, OpenAs("ben", dojoBen, dojoBody, dojoKeys));
Dojo.Eq("cy opens it", dojoMsg, OpenAs("cy", dojoCy, dojoBody, dojoKeys));
Dojo.Check("eve, not a recipient, gets null", OpenAs("eve", dojoEve, dojoBody, dojoKeys) is null, "eve opened it");
Dojo.Check("eve using ada's entry gets null", OpenAs("ada", dojoEve, dojoBody, dojoKeys) is null, "eve opened ada's copy");
var dojoMoved = new Dictionary<string, byte[]>(dojoKeys) { ["cy"] = dojoKeys["ben"] };
Dojo.Check("ben's wrap moved under cy's name is rejected", OpenAs("cy", dojoBen, dojoBody, dojoMoved) is null, "the label does not bind the name");
var dojoBad = (byte[])dojoBody.Clone();
dojoBad[^1] ^= 1;
Dojo.Check("a tampered body gives null", OpenAs("ada", dojoAda, dojoBad, dojoKeys) is null, "tampering went unnoticed");
hints: Write small helpers `GcmSeal(key, plain)` and `GcmOpen(key, nonce, tag, cipher)` and use them twice.
The content key is the *plaintext* of each recipient's wrap: 32 bytes in, 32 bytes of ciphertext out, plus the 91-byte ephemeral key, nonce and tag.

steps.title: Signed, sealed letters
prompt: Encryption alone does not say who sent a letter: anyone can encrypt to Bob's public key. Add a signature, and check it **before** decrypting.
`byte[] SealSigned(ECDsa sender, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey recipient, string message)`
- ephemeral-ECDH hybrid as in lesson 3: `[eph public 91][nonce 12][tag 16][ciphertext]`, AES key = HKDF-SHA256(shared, 32, info UTF-8 `"dojo-letter-v1"`);
- then append an ECDSA (SHA-256) signature of **everything before it**: 64 bytes at the end.
`string? OpenSigned(ECDiffieHellman recipient, ECDsa trustedSender, byte[] package)`
- return `null` if the package is shorter than 183 bytes, if the signature does not verify with `trustedSender`, or if decryption throws;
- otherwise the UTF-8 message.
starter: byte[] SealSigned(ECDsa sender, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey recipient, string message)
string? OpenSigned(ECDiffieHellman recipient, ECDsa trustedSender, byte[] package)
solution: byte[] SealSigned(ECDsa sender, ECDiffieHellmanPublicKey recipient, string message)

byte[] body = [.. eph.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo(), .. nonce, .. tag, .. cipher];

template: {{CODE}}
var dojoCurve = System.Security.Cryptography.ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256;
using var dojoAlice = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoMallory = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoBob = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
using var dojoCarol = System.Security.Cryptography.ECDiffieHellman.Create(dojoCurve);
var dojoPkg = SealSigned(dojoAlice, dojoBob.PublicKey, "Wire the deposit on Monday.");
Dojo.Eq("the package is 183 bytes plus the message", 183 + 27, dojoPkg.Length);
Dojo.Eq("Bob opens Alice's letter", "Wire the deposit on Monday.", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, dojoPkg));
var dojoForged = SealSigned(dojoMallory, dojoBob.PublicKey, "Wire the deposit to account 666.");
Dojo.Check("a letter signed by Mallory is rejected", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, dojoForged) is null, "accepted Mallory's forgery");
var dojoBad = (byte[])dojoPkg.Clone();
dojoBad[120] ^= 1;
Dojo.Check("a tampered ciphertext is rejected", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, dojoBad) is null, "accepted a tampered letter");
var dojoBadSig = (byte[])dojoPkg.Clone();
dojoBadSig[^1] ^= 1;
Dojo.Check("a damaged signature is rejected", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, dojoBadSig) is null, "accepted a damaged signature");
Dojo.Check("Carol cannot read Bob's letter", OpenSigned(dojoCarol, dojoAlice, dojoPkg) is null, "Carol decrypted it");
Dojo.Check("a truncated package is rejected", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, dojoPkg[..100]) is null, "accepted 100 bytes");
Dojo.Eq("an empty letter works", "", OpenSigned(dojoBob, dojoAlice, SealSigned(dojoAlice, dojoBob.PublicKey, "")));
hints: Build `body` first, sign it, and return `[.. body, .. signature]`.
In `OpenSigned`, split with `package[..^64]` and `package[^64..]`, verify, and only then decrypt inside a `try`.
